groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The sports hall hummed with tension as the final minutes of the inter-school floorball championships ticked away. Wei Han had __(16: conscientiously)__ practised his shots every afternoon under the scorching sun at the school's floorball court, and now all those hours of training were about to be put to the test. Facing a __(17: formidable)__ defence from the opposing team, whose exceptional skills had helped them remain undefeated all season, he refused to back down. Despite his aching limbs, Wei Han's __(18: resilience)__ kept him sprinting towards the goal.
With seconds left, he __(19: caught sight of)__ the goalkeeper leaning slightly to the left. He made a shrewd move, pretending he was __(20: going for)__ a high shot before sliding the ball into the opposite corner. Wei Han cheered elatedly as the whistle blew and his teammates swarmed around him in jubilant celebration. It was a victory that proved determination was the key to success.

Study the poster for a school bag (Text 1) and the extract taken from an online article (Text 2) and answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below shows an advertisement for a bag.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from an online article.
School bags are essential for students, but choosing the right one and packing it wisely can protect your back while keeping you comfortable, organised and healthy every school day ahead.
While it may seem convenient to fit everything into one bag, have you considered the weight? Carrying too many items strains your back. This may cause short-term discomfort and lead to long-term posture problems. To cushion the effect, you should carry a school bag that fits comfortably on your back. Features such as wide straps and padded backs help distribute weight more evenly. By choosing a school bag wisely, you can reduce the pressure on your back.
Ultimately, health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day to keep your school bag light. For example, store certain items in your school locker or keep some materials under your desk if your school allows it. By planning what you bring each day and leaving out unnecessary items, you can protect your back and still have everything you need.

images.alt: Advertisement with a picture of a backpack in the middle. Heading: Peaks School Bag. Slogan: Carry Everything in Style. Text: Say goodbye to boring school bags. Fit your entire school day into one bag — all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more! Get organised with a specific space for everything. Left of the bag: Suitable for students of all ages! Right of the bag: Wide range of colours to choose from! Below the bag: Designed with you in mind! Bottom banner with a picture of a smiling schoolboy carrying a bag: "I love my Peaks school bag! Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it. I can also find and take out any item I need easily!" – Ansel, primary school student

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

Every day, we enjoy fruit without realising how many quiet changes have taken place inside them. The mystery behind fruit ripening __(26)__ still not fully understood by scientists and farmers. Most fruits are picked when they are still firm and green, as they bruise easily __(27)__ left to ripen fully on the tree. The flesh of these fruits __(28)__ been known to contain a gas called ethylene which acts as a signal to begin __(29)__ ripening process. Ethylene spreads through the cells and reaches the parts __(30)__ the seeds develop. As the level of ethylene rises, the fruit softens, turns sweeter and changes colour.
In storage rooms, workers __(31)__ slow down the ripening process __(32)__ keeping the fruits cool and reducing the amount of ethylene in the air. Later, to speed up the ripening process, they may place unripe fruits into closed boxes with a few ripe bananas __(33)__ have already released a lot of ethylene. Similarly, people sometimes put __(34)__ unripe mango in a paper bag with a ripe banana because this simple trick speeds up the ripening process. Scientists are still studying the process of fruit ripening in the hope __(35)__ using this knowledge to reduce food waste and to keep fruit fresh for a longer period.
The next time you watch a hard, green fruit slowly turn soft and sweet, you are witnessing this hidden ripening process at work.

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

It was Jia Wei's first day back in school. He had already regretted __(36: volentiering)__ for the student council project. He and three classmates were tasked __(37: by)__ planning an exhibition on Singapore's __(38: enviromantle)__ efforts. The principal also made it clear that everyone __(39: are)__ expected to do a good job. As Jia Wei __(40: skrold)__ through old photographs of the Singapore Harbour, he noticed one depicting a coastline that looked nothing like the present one. The caption said it was taken before land reclamation had __(41: begin)__ in the area. He felt a sudden urge to find out what the town might lose if people only cared about __(42: sprauling)__ shopping malls and new MRT lines. __(43: Although)__, his friends were far more __(44: in··erested)__ in designing beautiful posters instead of checking their facts. After a long discussion, the group still had no clear concept. Walking home, Jia Wei realised __(45: what)__ easily a city's memories could disappear beneath glass and concrete. The thought stayed with him long after he reached home.

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

Zubir Said was the composer who wrote Majulah Singapura, the national anthem of Singapore. Born in 1907 in Sumatra, Zubir grew up in a poor household where money was always __(46)__ enough but music was always present. __(47)__ a teenager, he left home and sailed to Singapore. His __(48)__ from childhood was to become a professional musician. The first __(49)__ he had was playing the violin and piano in silent movie theatres, bringing the film to __(50)__ with his music. The work was tiring and the pay was low, but these early experiences honed his skills and confidence as a composer.
In 1958, the City Council of Singapore invited him to come __(51)__ with a special song for a civic celebration. He __(52)__ the task readily. He walked along crowded streets and quiet kampungs, __(53)__ inspiration for the perfect song. He __(54)__ the song to capture the aspirations of a young nation – its courage, unity and hope. After many revisions, he composed a rousing __(55)__ that ordinary people could remember and sing with pride. After Singapore became independent, the song was __(56)__ by the government as the national anthem of Singapore.
Although he did not study at prestigious music schools, Zubir kept improving his musical technique, striving to be a better composer than __(57)__ before. He believed that a national anthem __(58)__ not only sound grand but also encourage citizens to serve their country and care for one another.
Today, students sing Majulah Singapura during assemblies and at national __(59)__ like the Primary 5 National Education (NE) Show so that they show their __(60)__ for the sacrifices and dreams that helped build Singapore. His creation continues to spur young people to contribute in their own ways to the nation.

Read the passage and answer questions 66 to 75 in complete sentences.

**1** Maya had always admired her grandfather's magnificent lettuce garden, which was truly the apple of his eye. It stretched across the entire back corner of their family property. Every morning at precisely six o'clock, she watched him tend to his prized lettuce with meticulous care, treating each plant with the gentle attention of a devoted parent nurturing his child. When her grandfather fell ill and had to stay in hospital for two weeks, Maya's heart sank as she saw her dear grandfather's plants beginning to wilt under the relentless scorching sun.
**2** "Mum, can I take care of Grandfather's garden while he's away?" Maya asked earnestly, her voice trembling with emotion. Her mother gave her a concerned look. "Are you sure you want to do it? This would be a big responsibility, Maya. Plants need daily attention, you know? It'll be **an uphill task** for you."
**3** The next morning, Maya woke up early and rushed eagerly to the garden with nervous excitement fluttering wildly in her stomach like trapped butterflies. Although she had watched her grandfather's practised movements countless times, doing it herself the first time felt like an arduous task. The metal watering can was heavier than expected, and she was not sure how much water each plant actually needed. After soaking the thirsty plants thoroughly, she noticed the lettuce leaves looking droopy despite her efforts, making her feel deeply worried.
**4** Feeling extremely discouraged, Maya called her best friend, Sandie, for advice. "My grandmother grows vegetables too! Let me ask her for her opinion," Sandie offered without hesitation. Within an hour, Sandie arrived breathlessly with her elderly grandmother, Mrs Chen, who began to examine the struggling garden with the sharp, keen eye of an experienced gardener.
**5** "You're doing remarkably well, dear! However, different plants need different amounts of water," Mrs Chen said with a smile. "For example, the soil for lettuce should not be too wet. Gardening requires patience. **Rome wasn't built in a day, and neither is a beautiful garden.**"
**6** Over the next few days, Maya took Sandie's grandmother's advice to heart, taking special care not to overwater the lettuce. Sandie often joined her, and together, they removed stubborn weeds and dead leaves, making the demanding work considerably easier and much more enjoyable. Sandie discovered that the plants grew faster after they talked to them, though Maya suspected **it** was just coincidence.
**7** When some destructive aphids suddenly attacked the vulnerable lettuce plants, Maya's heart raced frantically. However, she refused to give up. Instead, she researched for natural remedies online and prepared a soap solution. Then she sprinkled the treatment onto the affected leaves. She felt immensely proud watching the tiny green invaders disappear completely after **that treatment**. The garden slowly transformed from wilting to thriving under her dedicated care, flourishing beautifully once again.
**8** Two weeks later, Maya's grandfather returned home to find his lettuce garden more beautiful than ever, a truly wonderful sight after his hospital stay. Tears of joy streamed down his cheeks as he saw the healthy plants and Maya's detailed notebook filled with careful observations. "You've done **something wonderful** here," he said, pointing at the garden.
**9** "Sandie helped me a lot, and Mrs Chen taught us so much," Maya replied modestly, her cheeks glowing with pride. "I never knew gardening required such dedication."
**10** Her grandfather smiled knowingly, his eyes sparkling with happiness. "The best gardens grow from love and commitment, not just water and sunshine. Would you like to be my gardening partner from now on?" Maya's face lit up with pure joy as she nodded enthusiastically. Her mother nodded and gave her a thumbs-up.

questions.stem:
The pictures below show Ricky and Emily discussing an accident that happened during their school recess. Study the pictures carefully.
[[img1]]
++Your Task++
Imagine you are Ricky from Primary 6E.
**Write a report to your principal, Mdm Tan, to inform her about an accident that happened in school.**
You are to refer to the pictures and information on page 2 for your report. The bullet point underlined below requires you to come up with your own information.
In your report, include the following key information:
- what happened to Avery Lim
- what caused the accident
- when the accident happened
- where it happened
- ++one suggestion you have to prevent such an accident++
- why something must be done
You may reorder the points. Remember to write in complete sentences.

images.alt: Two comic panels dated 12 August 2026. A girl (Emily) and a boy (Ricky) stand near a water cooler with a puddle around it, between the school library and a staircase. Panel 1. Emily: Ricky, someone left the water cooler running again! Earlier in the day, during recess, our classmate, Avery Lim, slipped and fell because of a puddle on the floor. Ricky: That's terrible! What did you do to help? Emily: I turned off the water and helped Avery to the General Office so that the staff could see to her injury. Panel 2. Ricky: Something must be done. I may have an idea. Let me report this matter to our principal, and at the same time, make a suggestion so that our school can be a safer place for all our students and staff. Emily: You're such a proactive prefect! I hope things change for the better! Ricky: Thanks for the encouragement, Emily! I'll need your support!

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Purpose: to inform the principal about the accident (and to suggest how to prevent another one). State the purpose in your opening sentence.
Audience: Mdm Tan, your principal. Context: you are Ricky from Primary 6E, a prefect, writing about an accident in school.
Point 1, what happened to Avery Lim: she slipped and fell (and was injured; Emily helped her to the General Office).
Point 2, what caused the accident: someone left the water cooler running, so there was a puddle on the floor.
Point 3, when it happened: on 12 August 2026, during recess.
Point 4, where it happened: at the water cooler near the library (beside the staircase), as shown in the pictures.

Point 5, your own suggestion (the underlined point): one sensible idea, for example putting up a reminder sign at the water cooler, placing a non-slip mat there, or having prefects check the cooler during recess.
Point 6, why something must be done: so that the school can be a safer place for all students and staff.

Format and tone: a formal report or email. Start with 'Dear Mdm Tan', use polite, formal language (no contractions or slang), write in complete sentences and paragraphs, and sign off with 'Yours sincerely' / 'Yours respectfully', then 'Ricky' and 'Primary 6E'.
Do not copy Emily's speech as if you saw the accident yourself: Ricky heard about it from Emily, so report it accurately in the past tense.

review.keyAnswer: No answer key is provided for Paper 1.
review.solvedAnswer: Checklist written from the task and pictures.
review.note: The task is not numbered on the paper (Part 1); it is recorded as Question 1. Faint pencil marks from a previous owner (a '3', a tick and a '6') are visible on the stimulus; they do not affect the task. The place of the accident is not stated in words; it is taken from the picture (water cooler outside the library, next to the staircase).

questions.stem:
Write a composition of ++at least 150 words++ about **showing respect**.
The pictures are provided to help you think about this topic.
Your composition should be based on one or more of these pictures.
[[img1]]
Consider the following points when you plan your composition:
- Why was there a need to show respect?
- How was respect shown?
You may use the points in any order and include other relevant points as well.

images.alt: Three pictures, one below the other. Picture 1: a wristwatch. Picture 2: a loudspeaker blasting loud music, with musical notes and lightning-shaped sound marks around it. Picture 3: a boy sitting with both hands covering his face.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Understand the topic: 'showing respect' means treating someone (or their time, feelings, property or needs) as important. Your story must show clearly WHY respect was needed and HOW it was shown.

Picture 1 (watch): respecting other people's time, for example being punctual for a team practice or an appointment instead of keeping others waiting; or respecting something precious, such as a grandparent's old watch.

Picture 2 (loudspeaker and music): being considerate about noise, for example turning down loud music for a neighbour who is ill, a baby who is sleeping or a sibling who is studying; or staying quiet during a performance or ceremony.
Picture 3 (boy covering his face): respecting someone's feelings, for example not laughing at or teasing a classmate who is upset or embarrassed, giving him space, listening and comforting him.
Use at least one picture and make it important to the plot, not just mentioned in passing.

Story arc: an opening that sets the scene; a problem in which someone is NOT shown respect (or it is hard to show it); a turning point where the main character realises why respect is needed; the action that shows respect; the result.
Show feelings and thoughts with actions and dialogue ('my cheeks burned', 'I lowered the volume and knocked on his door') instead of just telling.
Ending: return to the topic with a reflection, for example what the character learnt about respect and how he or she behaves differently now.
Check: at least 150 words, paragraphs, consistent past tense, and both guiding points answered.

review.keyAnswer: No answer key is provided for Paper 1.
review.solvedAnswer: Planning checklist written from the topic and pictures.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
"They've never been to the theatres in Singapore, __________?" Aunt Mona asked.

explanation: Rule: a question tag uses the same helping verb as the statement. A positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag.
'They've' is short for 'They have', so the helping verb is 'have'. That rules out 'did they' and 'didn't they'.
'never' makes the statement negative, so the tag must be positive: 'have they', not 'haven't they'.
The answer is option (2), have they.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
The detective was __________ the verge of giving up when he discovered the hidden clue in a dusty diary.

explanation: 'on the verge of' is a fixed phrase. It means very close to doing something.
The detective had almost given up when he found the clue.
The other prepositions do not go with 'the verge of'; 'in' is tempting because of phrases such as 'in the middle of', but the phrase is always 'on the verge of'.
The answer is option (3), on.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
When the old man dropped his groceries, several kind strangers helped him __________ them up from the pavement.

explanation: Rule: help + someone + base form of the verb (with or without 'to'): 'helped him pick' or 'helped him to pick'.
The tense is already shown by 'helped', so the second verb does not change.
'picked' is tempting because the sentence is in the past, but only the first verb carries the past tense.
The answer is option (1), pick.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
Paul giggled softly when he saw his grandmother talking to __________ while watching her favourite drama on television.

explanation: Rule: use a reflexive pronoun (-self) when the doer and the receiver of the action are the same person.
The grandmother was doing the talking, and she was talking to nobody else: she was talking to herself while watching 'her' favourite drama.
'her' would mean another woman, and 'himself' does not match 'grandmother', who is female.
The answer is option (3), herself.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
__________ the noise from the construction work nearby, the children managed to concentrate on their lessons.

explanation: Look at the two ideas: there was noise, yet the children managed to concentrate. The second idea is a surprise, so we need a connector of contrast.
'In spite of' + noun means 'although there was'.

'Owing to' and 'As a result of' give a cause, but noise does not cause concentration. 'Contrary to' means 'opposite to what was said or expected', as in 'contrary to popular belief', and does not fit with 'the noise'.
The answer is option (2), In spite of.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
Even though he practised for weeks before the school concert, Marcus still had __________ confidence when he walked onto the stage to perform his solo.

explanation: 'Even though ... still' signals a surprise: he practised for weeks, yet he did not feel confident.
'confidence' is uncountable. 'little' (without 'a') is used with uncountable nouns and means 'hardly any'.
'few' is only for countable nouns. 'some' and 'much' would mean he was confident, which is no surprise after weeks of practice.
The answer is option (2), little.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
By the time the school bell rang, all the students __________ their art projects and placed them on display.

explanation: Rule: 'By the time' + simple past is followed by the past perfect (had + past participle) for the action that was completed earlier.
The finishing happened before the bell rang, so: 'had finished'. ('placed' shares the same 'had': had finished ... and placed.)
'finished' is tempting, but it does not show that the action was already complete before the bell. 'have finished' is present perfect and cannot go with the past 'rang'.
The answer is option (3), had finished.

review.note: The key's digit for Q7 is partly under the watermark; the visible part is a 3, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
Jenna could not help __________ upon seeing her little brother trying to pull his hand out of the cookie jar.

explanation: Rule: 'could not help' (meaning 'could not stop oneself') is followed by the -ing form of the verb.
Jenna could not stop herself from laughing: 'could not help laughing'.
'to laugh' is tempting because 'help to do' exists, but that means 'assist', which is a different meaning.
The answer is option (3), laughing.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
This mystery novel is by far __________ one I have read this year.

explanation: 'by far' is used to stress a superlative: it means 'by a great amount'.
The novel is compared with all the books read this year (more than two), so we need the superlative: 'the most exciting'.
'the more exciting' is used when comparing only two things.
The answer is option (3), the most exciting.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
"Where __________ the pair of glasses that I placed on the desk this morning?" wondered Mrs Lim.

explanation: Find the subject: 'the pair of glasses'. The head word is 'pair', which is singular, so the verb is singular. That rules out 'are' and 'were'.
Mrs Lim is wondering now where the glasses are at this moment, so the verb is in the present tense: 'is'.
'was' is tempting because 'placed' is in the past, but only the placing happened in the morning; the looking is happening now.
The answer is option (1), is.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
A fight __________ on the football field when two students started quarrelling over the yellow card issued by the referee.

explanation: 'broke out' means started suddenly. It is used for fights, fires, wars and diseases.
The fight started when the two students quarrelled, so 'A fight broke out'.
'broke up' means ended or separated (a teacher breaks up a fight), which is the opposite. 'broke off' means stopped suddenly or snapped off; 'broke down' means stopped working.
The answer is option (3), broke out.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
After months of hard work, Maria became __________ playing the piano and could perform complex pieces without making mistakes.

explanation: Clues: 'months of hard work' and 'could perform complex pieces without making mistakes'. She became very skilled.
'proficient at' means skilled and able to do something very well.

'familiar with' is tempting, but it only means knowing something fairly well, not being highly skilled. 'certified in' means holding an official certificate, and 'inspired by' does not fit the result of hard work.
The answer is option (3), proficient at.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
Sarah looked __________ at the tall diving board, worried about jumping into the deep water for the first time.

explanation: Clue: she was 'worried about jumping into the deep water'.
'apprehensively' means in a worried or nervous way about something that is going to happen.
'quizzically' means in a puzzled, questioning way; 'reproachfully' means in a blaming way; 'cynically' means in a distrusting way. None of these shows worry.
The answer is option (4), apprehensively.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
Siti could hardly __________ her emotions upon hearing the devastating news.

explanation: 'suppress' means to hold back a feeling so that it does not show. We 'suppress' emotions, tears, a smile or a yawn.
The news was devastating, so Siti could hardly hold back her feelings.
'restrict' is tempting, but it means to limit the amount or movement of something (restrict the number of visitors). 'omit' means leave out; 'reduce' means make smaller.
The answer is option (4), suppress.

questions.stem:
Choose the answer that best fits in the sentence.
The storm began to __________ as the wind grew stronger and the rain became heavier throughout the afternoon.

explanation: Clues: 'the wind grew stronger and the rain became heavier'. The storm became stronger.
'intensify' means to become stronger or more extreme.
'accelerate' is tempting, but it means to go faster, and the clues are about strength, not speed. 'advance' means move forward; 'maximise' means make as large as possible and needs an object.
The answer is option (1), intensify.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++conscientiously++.

explanation: 'conscientiously' means carefully and with great effort, because you want to do something well.
Clue in the passage: he practised 'every afternoon under the scorching sun' for hours.
'diligently' means in a hard-working and careful way, which matches.
'precisely' means exactly; 'frantically' means in a hurried, panicky way; 'haphazardly' means without any plan, which is the opposite. The answer is option (1).

review.note: The key's digit for Q16 is mostly under the watermark; the visible stroke is a 1, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++formidable++.

explanation: 'formidable' describes something so strong or powerful that it is very hard to deal with.
Clue: the opposing team had 'exceptional skills' and was 'undefeated all season', so their defence was very hard to beat.
'tough' means difficult to beat or get through, which matches a defence best.

'frightening' is tempting because formidable things can cause fear, but the passage is about how strong the defence was, and Wei Han 'refused to back down'. 'tremendous' means very great in size or amount. The answer is option (2).

review.note: The key's digit for Q17 is partly under the watermark; the visible part is a 2, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++resilience++.

explanation: 'resilience' is the ability to keep going and not give up when things are hard.
Clue: 'Despite his aching limbs' he kept sprinting, and the last line says 'determination was the key to success'.
'persistence' means continuing to try in spite of difficulty, which matches.
'stamina' is tempting, but it is physical energy to keep going for a long time; his limbs were already aching, so it was his will, not his energy, that kept him going. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++caught sight of++.

explanation: 'caught sight of' means suddenly saw something, often for a moment.
He saw the goalkeeper leaning slightly to the left.
'noticed' means saw or became aware of, which matches.
'scanned' means looked over an area carefully to search for something, which is a longer, deliberate action. The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++going for++.

explanation: To 'go for' something means to try to get or achieve it, or to aim at it. Here Wei Han pretended that he was aiming at a high shot.
'pursuing' means trying to achieve something, which is the dictionary meaning nearest to 'going for'.
'faking' does not work when swapped in: the sentence already says 'pretending', and 'pretending he was faking a high shot' would mean the opposite of what happened.
The solved answer is option (3). The school's key gives option (1), so check this question with a teacher.

review.note: Key says (1) faking; solved answer is (3) pursuing. Substituting 'faking' gives 'pretending he was faking a high shot', which does not keep the meaning, so the key looks wrong. However, none of the remaining options is a clean synonym: (2) planning and (4) executing can also be argued. A parent or teacher should decide.

questions.stem: The purpose of the statement "Carry Everything in Style" in Text 1 is to __________.
options: highlight that the bag is useful and trendy
command students to care about how they look
remind students about what they must bring to school

explanation: Break the slogan into its two ideas. 'Carry Everything' says the bag can hold all you need, so it is useful. 'in Style' says it looks fashionable, so it is trendy.
The poster backs up both ideas: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag' and 'Say goodbye to boring school bags'.
(1) is tempting, but it covers only the 'Carry Everything' half and leaves out 'in Style'.
The answer is option (2).

review.note: A previous owner pencilled faint question labels ('Q21', 'Q2…') above the slogan on the poster. They mark where to look, not the answer, so the crop is kept.

questions.stem: Ansel was quoted in Text 1 because __________.
options: he appears to be a good student
all school bag users are around his age
his review was short enough to fit into the poster
what he said supports the claims made in the poster

explanation: Advertisements quote users (a testimonial) to convince readers that what the advertisement says is true.

Match Ansel's words to the poster's claims: 'Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it' supports 'Fit your entire school day into one bag'; 'I can also find and take out any item I need easily' supports 'Get organised with a specific space for everything'.
(2) is false because the poster says the bag is 'Suitable for students of all ages'.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem:
Based on Text 1, which of the following statements are true about the Peaks school bag?
A. The bag is small and light.
B. The bag comes in different colours.
C. The bag has multiple compartments.

explanation: A: the poster never says the bag is small or light. It says you can 'Fit your entire school day into one bag', which suggests a roomy bag. A is not supported.
B: 'Wide range of colours to choose from!' So B is true.
C: 'Get organised with a specific space for everything', and Ansel can 'find and take out any item' easily. Separate spaces for different things are compartments. So C is true.
The answer is option (3), B and C.

questions.stem: What is the **main** message of Text 2?
options: Students should take measures to protect their backs.
Students should choose school bags with padded backs.
Students should fit everything into one bag for convenience.
Students should use lockers and desks to store their belongings.

explanation: The main message is the idea that runs through the whole text, not one detail.
Every paragraph of Text 2 comes back to the back: 'can protect your back', 'reduce the pressure on your back', 'you can protect your back and still have everything you need'.
(2) and (4) are true details, but each is only one way of protecting the back (choosing the bag wisely; packing light). (3) is the idea that Text 2 warns against.
The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Text 1 and Text 2 express differing views on whether __________.
options: students should store certain items in school
school bags should look appealing to students
students should fit everything into their school bags
school bags should be designed with students in mind

explanation: 'Differing views' means both texts talk about the same thing but do not agree.
Text 1 encourages it: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag — all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more!'
Text 2 questions it: 'While it may seem convenient to fit everything into one bag, have you considered the weight?' and recommends 'packing only the items needed for the day'.
The other options are each mentioned in only one text, so the texts cannot disagree on them. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The subject is 'The mystery behind fruit ripening'. The head word is 'mystery', which is singular.
After the blank is 'still not fully understood by scientists': this is the passive voice (be + past participle).
'still' shows the situation is true now, so the verb is present tense: 'is', not 'was'.
The answer is (J) is: 'The mystery ... is still not fully understood'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence gives a condition: the fruits bruise easily in one situation, namely when they are left to ripen on the tree.
'if left to ripen' is a short form of 'if they are left to ripen'. 'if' can be followed directly by a past participle in this way.
The answer is (G) if: 'they bruise easily if left to ripen fully on the tree'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank is 'been known': the present perfect passive needs has/have + been + past participle.
The subject is 'The flesh of these fruits'. The head word is 'flesh' (singular), not 'fruits', so the verb is 'has', not 'have'.
The answer is (E) has: 'The flesh of these fruits has been known to contain a gas'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'ripening process' is a singular countable noun, so it needs a determiner in front.
It is a particular process that the reader already knows about (fruit ripening was introduced earlier), so we use the definite article 'the'.

'this' is tempting, but the process has not been pointed out in this sentence yet, and the passage uses the phrase 'the ripening process' again and again. 'a' does not fit because it is not just any process.
The answer is (L) the: 'a signal to begin the ripening process'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank joins 'the parts' to 'the seeds develop'. 'the parts' are places inside the fruit.
To add information about a place, use the relative adverb 'where' (= in which).
'which' is tempting, but 'the parts which the seeds develop' would mean the seeds develop the parts. The seeds develop IN those parts.
The answer is (P) where: 'reaches the parts where the seeds develop'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank is the base verb 'slow down' with the plural subject 'workers'. A modal verb fits before a base verb.
'can' shows what the workers are able to do.
The answer is (D) can: 'workers can slow down the ripening process'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The words after the blank tell us HOW the workers slow the process down: 'keeping the fruits cool and reducing the amount of ethylene'.
Rule: by + verb-ing shows the method used to do something.
The answer is (C) by: 'by keeping the fruits cool'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank joins 'a few ripe bananas' to 'have already released a lot of ethylene'. It stands for the bananas and is the subject of 'have released'.
For things, the relative pronoun is 'which' (or 'that').
'where' is for places and cannot be the subject of a verb, so it belongs in blank (30), not here.
The answer is (Q) which: 'a few ripe bananas which have already released a lot of ethylene'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'unripe mango' is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time, so it needs 'a' or 'an'.
'unripe' begins with a vowel sound (un-), so the article is 'an', not 'a'.
The answer is (B) an: 'put an unripe mango in a paper bag'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'in the hope of' + verb-ing is a fixed phrase meaning 'wishing that something will happen'.
After the blank is 'using', an -ing form, which follows the preposition 'of'.
The answer is (K) of: 'in the hope of using this knowledge'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++volentiering++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Say the word in parts: vol-un-teer-ing.
The middle sound is 'un', spelt with a 'u', and the ending is '-teer' with a double 'e' (like engineer and pioneer).
After 'regretted', the -ing form is correct, so only the spelling changes.
The correct word is 'volunteering'.

review.keyAnswer: (vol)unteering — the first letters are under the watermark
review.note: Two letters of the printed misspelling are rubbed out in the scan ('vo·entie·ing'); it is transcribed as 'volentiering' from the visible letters. The start of the key's answer is under the watermark ('...entering' visible, i.e. volunteering), which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++by++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong preposition.
The verb 'task' takes 'with': to be tasked with (doing) something means to be given that job.
'by' would introduce the person who gave the task (tasked by the principal), but here what follows is the job itself: 'planning an exhibition'.
The correct word is 'with'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++enviromantle++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Start from the base word 'environment': en-vi-ron-ment. Do not forget the 'n' before 'ment'.
Add the adjective ending '-al': environment + al = environmental.
The ending sounds like 'tle' but is spelt '-tal'.
The correct word is 'environmental'.

review.note: Some letters of the printed misspelling are rubbed out in the scan; it is transcribed as 'enviromantle' from the visible letters.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++are++.

explanation: This is a grammar error with two things to fix: agreement and tense.
Agreement: 'everyone' is always singular, so it cannot take 'are'.
Tense: the story is told in the past ('The principal also made it clear that ...'), so the verb is past tense.
The correct word is 'was': 'everyone was expected to do a good job'.

review.note: The key's label for Q39 is under the watermark, but the answer 'was' is clear.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++skrold++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The base word is 'scroll': the /sk/ sound is spelt 'sc', and it ends in double 'l'.
Add '-ed' for the past tense: scroll + ed = scrolled.
The correct word is 'scrolled'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++begin++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the helping verb in front: 'had ___'.
Rule: had + past participle makes the past perfect tense.
The verb forms are begin, began, begun. The past participle is 'begun' ('began' is the simple past and cannot follow 'had').
The correct word is 'begun'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++sprauling++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The /aw/ sound in this word is spelt 'aw', as in 'crawl' and 'shawl'.
'sprawling' means spreading out over a large area, which describes huge shopping malls.
The correct word is 'sprawling'.

review.note: One letter of the printed misspelling is rubbed out in the scan; it is transcribed as 'sprauling' from the visible letters.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++Although++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong kind of connector.
'Although' joins two clauses in one sentence and is never followed by a comma on its own.

Here the word starts a new sentence, is followed by a comma, and shows a contrast with the sentence before (Jia Wei cared about what the town might lose, but his friends cared about posters). That is the job of 'However'.
The correct word is 'However'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++in··erested++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. Say the word in parts: in-ter-est-ed.
'interested in' means wanting to know about or do something: his friends were 'far more interested in designing beautiful posters'.
The correct word is 'interested'.

review.note: The middle letters of the printed misspelling are rubbed out in the scan and cannot be read (shown as 'in··erested'). The correct word is certainly 'interested' (key and solved answer agree); only the transcription of the wrong word is incomplete.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++what++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. The word is followed by the adverb 'easily'.
Rule: use 'how' + adjective/adverb to talk about degree: 'how easily', 'how quickly', 'how tall'.
'what' is followed by a noun (what a pity, what memories), not by an adverb.
The correct word is 'how': 'realised how easily a city's memories could disappear'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clue: Zubir grew up in 'a poor household', so there was very little money.
The blank comes between 'always' and 'enough', so it must be an adverb that describes 'enough'. 'barely enough' means only just enough, almost not enough.
'hardly enough' and 'scarcely enough' mean the same.
'but music was always present' gives the contrast: little money, plenty of music. The answer is 'barely'.

review.note: The key gives 'scarce', but 'money was always scarce enough' is not grammatical: an adverb is needed before 'enough' (barely / hardly / scarcely enough). The key probably intends 'scarcely'. The solved answer 'barely' is set as the answer; 'hardly', 'scarcely' and the key's 'scarce' are also accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: '___ a teenager, he left home' tells us what he was at the time he left.
'As a teenager' means 'when he was a teenager'. 'As' + noun is used for a role or stage of life.
The answer is 'As'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence says what he had wanted 'from childhood': 'to become a professional musician'.
Something a person has long wished to become is a dream or an ambition.
The answer is 'dream'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is described by what follows: 'playing the violin and piano in silent movie theatres'.
The next sentence says 'The work was tiring and the pay was low', so this was paid work: a job.
The answer is 'job'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'bring something to life' is a fixed phrase meaning to make something exciting and real.
Silent films had no sound, so his music made them come alive for the audience.
The answer is 'life'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'come up with' is a phrasal verb meaning to think of or produce an idea, a plan or a piece of work.
The City Council asked him to produce a special song: 'come up with a special song'.
The answer is 'up'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: He was 'invited' to do something, and the sentence says he did so 'readily' (willingly, without delay).
The verb that goes with an invitation or a task you agree to do is 'accept'. The story is in the past, so 'accepted'.
The answer is 'accepted'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: Why did he walk along the streets and kampungs? To look for ideas, that is, inspiration.
The blank follows a comma and has no subject, so it is an -ing form that describes what he was doing as he walked.
'seeking' means looking for, and it takes an object directly: 'seeking inspiration'. ('looking' would need 'for', and only one word is allowed.)
The answer is 'seeking'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: Pattern: verb + object + to-infinitive: 'He ___ the song to capture the aspirations of a young nation'.
'want something to do something' fits this pattern and tells us his aim. The story is in the past, so 'wanted'.
The answer is 'wanted'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: What does a composer compose that people can 'remember and sing'? A tune or melody.
'rousing' means stirring and exciting, which describes music.
The answer is 'tune' (or 'melody').

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: Pattern: 'was ___ by the government as the national anthem'. This is the passive voice, so a past participle is needed.
To 'adopt' something means to choose it officially and start using it.
The answer is 'adopted'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'than ever before' is a fixed phrase meaning 'than at any time in the past'.
He kept improving, so he was trying to be a better composer than he had been at any earlier time.
The answer is 'ever'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: After the blank are the base verbs 'sound' and 'encourage' with a singular subject ('a national anthem'). Without a modal verb they would need an -s, so a modal fits.
The sentence gives his belief about what an anthem ought to do. 'should' expresses what is right or expected.
The answer is 'should'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: An example is given straight after the blank: 'like the Primary 5 National Education (NE) Show'.
A show like that is an organised happening for the nation: a national event. The blank is plural because it stands for many of them.
The answer is 'events'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: Students sing the anthem to 'show their ___ for the sacrifices and dreams that helped build Singapore'.
What we feel and show for other people's sacrifices is thankfulness: appreciation or gratitude. Both take the preposition 'for'.
The answer is 'appreciation'.

questions.stem:
None of the plates in the sink is clean.
All ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: All the plates in the sink are dirty.
accept: All of the plates in the sink are dirty.

explanation: 'None ... is clean' means not a single plate is clean. Starting with 'All' turns the sentence round, so the describing word must change to its opposite: clean becomes dirty.
Agreement: 'All the plates' is plural, so the verb changes from 'is' to 'are'.
Do not write 'All the plates are not clean': that can also mean 'only some are clean', so the meaning is no longer the same.
Answer: All the plates in the sink are dirty.

review.keyAnswer: All the plates in the sink are dirty.
review.solvedAnswer: All (of) the plates in the sink are dirty.

questions.stem:
The chef works very hard but he cannot perfect the new recipe.
However ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.

explanation: Here 'However' is not the connector meaning 'but'. 'However + adjective/adverb + subject + verb' means 'no matter how ...'.
Take the adverb 'hard' and put it straight after 'However'. Drop 'very' (the idea of degree is already in 'however') and drop 'but'.
Put a comma after the first clause, then write the main clause unchanged.
Name the chef in the first clause and use 'he' in the second. Answer: However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.

review.keyAnswer: However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.
review.solvedAnswer: However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.

questions.stem:
Father reminded Lisa, "Do your homework before meeting your friends."
Lisa was reminded ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.
accept: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before she met her friends.
Lisa was reminded by her father to do her homework before meeting her friends.

explanation: Two changes are needed: active to passive voice, and direct to reported speech.
Passive: Lisa becomes the subject, and the doer follows 'by': 'Lisa was reminded by Father'.
A reported instruction uses 'to' + base verb: 'Do your homework' becomes 'to do her homework'.
Pronouns change to fit Lisa: 'your' becomes 'her' both times.
Answer: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.

review.keyAnswer: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.
review.solvedAnswer: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.

questions.stem:
Children can benefit from regular exercise.
Exercising ____________________ for children.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Exercising regularly is beneficial for children.
accept: Exercising regularly can be beneficial for children.

explanation: The sentence now starts with the gerund 'Exercising' (a verb used as a noun), so the other words must change their forms to fit.
'regular' described the noun 'exercise'. To describe the verb form 'exercising', use the adverb: 'regularly'.
'benefit' was a verb. After 'is' (or 'can be') and before 'for children', use the adjective: 'beneficial'.
A gerund subject is singular, so the verb is 'is'. Answer: Exercising regularly is beneficial for children.

review.keyAnswer: Exercising regularly is beneficial for children.
review.solvedAnswer: Exercising regularly is (can be) beneficial for children.
review.note: The printed answer line ends with 'for children.', so the blank is in the middle. 'can be beneficial' keeps the 'can' of the given sentence and is also accepted.

questions.stem:
You can place the ice cubes in the container after you break them up.
It is only after breaking up the ice cubes ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: It is only after breaking up the ice cubes that you can place them in the container.

explanation: The pattern 'It is only after ... that ...' stresses the condition that must come first.
After 'It is only after + -ing phrase', the main clause is introduced by 'that'.
'the ice cubes' has already been named in the starter, so use the pronoun 'them' in the main clause.
Answer: It is only after breaking up the ice cubes that you can place them in the container.

review.keyAnswer: It is only after breaking up the ice cubes that you can place them in the container.
review.solvedAnswer: It is only after breaking up the ice cubes that you can place them in the container.

questions.stem: Pick out a four-word phrase from the first paragraph which tells us that Maya's grandfather cherished the lettuce garden.

explanation: To 'cherish' something is to love it and treat it as precious.
Paragraph 1 says the garden 'was truly the apple of his eye'. The idiom 'the apple of someone's eye' means the thing or person that someone loves most.
Count exactly four words and copy them without changing anything: apple (1) of (2) his (3) eye (4). Leave out 'the', or the phrase has five words.
The answer is 'apple of his eye'.

questions.stem:
Circle one word that best describes how Maya felt when she saw her grandfather's plants wilting. DO NOT CIRCLE MORE THAN ONE WORD.
frustrated     guilty     dismayed     anxious
(Type the word you would circle.)

explanation: Find the moment in paragraph 1: 'Maya's heart sank as she saw her dear grandfather's plants beginning to wilt'.
When your 'heart sinks', you suddenly feel sad and disappointed at something unpleasant. That is what 'dismayed' means.

'anxious' is tempting, but it means worried about what might happen; 'heart sank' shows sadness at what she saw. She had not done anything wrong, so she was not 'guilty', and she had not tried and failed yet, so she was not 'frustrated'.
The answer is 'dismayed'.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, give two reasons why Maya's mother said it would be "an uphill task" when Maya asked to take care of the garden.

answer.value: Maya's mother said so because taking care of the garden would be a big responsibility and because plants need daily attention.

explanation: An 'uphill task' is one that is very difficult. Look at what Mother said just before those words.
Reason 1 (1 mark): 'This would be a big responsibility, Maya.'
Reason 2 (1 mark): 'Plants need daily attention, you know?'
Give both reasons in a complete sentence. One reason alone earns only one mark.

review.keyAnswer: It was a big responsibility and the plants needed daily attention.
review.solvedAnswer: It would be a big responsibility, and plants need daily attention. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Write 1, 2 and 3 in the blanks below to indicate the order in which the events occurred in the story.
___ Maya's grandfather fell ill and was hospitalised.
___ Mrs Chen taught Maya how to take care of plants.
___ Maya decided to take care of her grandfather's plants.
(Type the three numbers in the order of the statements, for example: 3, 1, 2.)

explanation: Find each event in the passage and note its paragraph.
Grandfather fell ill and stayed in hospital: paragraph 1. This is first (1).
Maya asked her mother if she could take care of the garden: paragraph 2. This is second (2).
Mrs Chen came and gave advice about watering: paragraph 5. This is third (3).
In the order of the statements, the numbers are 1, 3, 2.

review.keyAnswer: Grandfather was hospitalised — 1; Mrs Chen taught Maya — 3; Maya decided to care for the garden — 2

questions.stem: Based on the information from lines 10–26 (paragraphs 3 to 6), complete the following table.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How Maya felt when she saw the droopy lettuce leaves

answer.value: Maya felt deeply worried (and extremely discouraged).

explanation: Find the droopy leaves in paragraph 3: 'she noticed the lettuce leaves looking droopy despite her efforts, making her feel deeply worried.'
Paragraph 4 adds: 'Feeling extremely discouraged, Maya called her best friend'.
The marker looks for the feeling: deeply worried / extremely discouraged.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How Sandie responded upon hearing the problem

answer.value: Sandie offered without hesitation to ask her grandmother for her opinion, and within an hour she brought her grandmother, Mrs Chen, to Maya's garden to help.

explanation: Paragraph 4: '"My grandmother grows vegetables too! Let me ask her for her opinion," Sandie offered without hesitation.'
She then acted on it: 'Within an hour, Sandie arrived breathlessly with her elderly grandmother, Mrs Chen'.
The marker looks for: she offered to ask her grandmother (and brought Mrs Chen over to help).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: What Mrs Chen taught Maya about watering plants

answer.value: Mrs Chen taught Maya that different plants need different amounts of water, and that the soil for lettuce should not be too wet.

explanation: Paragraph 5 gives Mrs Chen's words: 'different plants need different amounts of water' and 'the soil for lettuce should not be too wet'.
Maya had been 'soaking the thirsty plants thoroughly', so she had been giving the lettuce too much water.
The marker looks for: different plants need different amounts of water / lettuce soil should not be too wet.

parts.label: d

answer.value: Maya took Mrs Chen's advice to heart and took special care not to overwater the lettuce.

explanation: Paragraph 6: 'Maya took Sandie's grandmother's advice to heart, taking special care not to overwater the lettuce.'
'took the advice to heart' means she considered it seriously and followed it.
The marker looks for: she followed the advice and was careful not to overwater the lettuce.

review.keyAnswer: (a) Maya felt deeply worried / extremely discouraged. (b) Sandie offered to ask her grandmother and brought Mrs Chen to help. (c) Different plants need different amounts of water, and the soil for lettuce should not be too wet. (d) Maya took the advice to heart and made sure that she did not overwater the lettuce.
review.solvedAnswer: Agrees with key on all four parts.
review.note: The printed table is a flow chart: (a) leads to (b), and (c) leads to (d). One mark per box.

questions.stem: Explain clearly what Mrs Chen meant when she said that "Rome wasn't built in a day, and neither is a beautiful garden." (line 22, paragraph 5)

answer.value: Mrs Chen meant that, just as the great city of Rome took a long time to build, a beautiful garden cannot be created quickly. It takes time, patience and steady care.

explanation: 'Rome wasn't built in a day' is a proverb: great things take a long time to achieve.
Idea 1 (1 mark): a beautiful garden cannot be created immediately or in a short time.
Idea 2 (1 mark): it needs time, patience and continued care. The clue is the sentence just before: 'Gardening requires patience.'
Explain the meaning for the garden; do not just repeat the proverb.

review.keyAnswer: A beautiful garden cannot be created immediately; it takes time, patience and steady care.
review.solvedAnswer: A beautiful garden, like Rome, cannot be made quickly; it takes time, patience and steady effort. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the word(s) in the left column refer(s) to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a

answer.value: Sandie's discovery that the plants grew faster after she and Maya talked to them.
accept: The plants growing faster after they talked to them.
The plants growing faster after Maya and Sandie talked to them.

explanation: A word like 'it' points back to something already mentioned. Read the first half of the sentence.
'Sandie discovered that the plants grew faster after they talked to them, though Maya suspected **it** was just coincidence.'
What did Maya think was a coincidence? The plants growing faster after the girls talked to them.
Test by replacing the word: 'Maya suspected the plants growing faster after they talked to them was just coincidence.' It makes sense.

parts.label: b

answer.value: The soap solution (that Maya prepared and sprinkled onto the affected leaves).
accept: The soap solution that Maya prepared.
The soap solution Maya sprinkled onto the affected leaves.

explanation: Read the sentences before 'that treatment' in paragraph 7.
'she ... prepared a soap solution. Then she sprinkled the treatment onto the affected leaves.' So the treatment is the soap solution.
Test by replacing the words: 'disappear completely after the soap solution' was sprinkled on. It makes sense.
The answer is the soap solution.

review.keyAnswer: (a) Sandie's observation that the plants seemed to grow faster when she and Maya talked to them. (b) the soap solution
review.solvedAnswer: (a) The plants growing faster after the girls talked to them. (b) The soap solution Maya sprinkled on the leaves. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on lines 10–31 (paragraphs 3 to 7), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Maya had no experience taking care of plants before her grandfather was hospitalised.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Although Maya had watched her grandfather's practised movements countless times, doing it herself for the first time felt like an arduous task.

explanation: Paragraph 3: 'Although she had watched her grandfather's practised movements countless times, doing it herself the first time felt like an arduous task.'
'the first time' shows she had only watched before and had never done it herself, so she had no experience.
So the statement is True. The reason must be evidence from the passage, not the statement repeated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Mrs Chen praised Maya for her efforts.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Mrs Chen told Maya, "You're doing remarkably well, dear!"

explanation: Paragraph 5 begins with Mrs Chen's words to Maya: 'You're doing remarkably well, dear!'
Telling someone she is doing 'remarkably well' is praise.
So the statement is True.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
Maya solved the aphid problem with help from Sandie and Mrs Chen.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Maya researched natural remedies online, prepared a soap solution and sprinkled it onto the affected leaves by herself.

explanation: Paragraph 7 describes the aphid attack. Every action is Maya's own: 'she researched for natural remedies online and prepared a soap solution. Then she sprinkled the treatment onto the affected leaves.'
Sandie and Mrs Chen are not mentioned in this paragraph. They helped with watering and weeding earlier, not with the aphids.
So the statement is False.

review.keyAnswer: (a) True — Although Maya had often watched her grandfather, caring for the plants herself for the first time felt arduous. (b) True — Mrs Chen told Maya that she was doing remarkably well. (c) False — Maya researched natural remedies and prepared and applied the soap solution herself.
review.solvedAnswer: (a) True; (b) True; (c) False, with the same reasons. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Maya's grandfather told her that she had done "something wonderful" (lines 34–35, paragraph 8). What did Maya do that was wonderful?

answer.value: Maya took care of her grandfather's lettuce garden while he was in hospital. She restored the wilting, aphid-attacked plants to health so that the garden was more beautiful than ever, and she kept a detailed notebook filled with careful observations.

explanation: Look at what Grandfather saw just before he spoke (paragraph 8): 'his lettuce garden more beautiful than ever', 'the healthy plants and Maya's detailed notebook filled with careful observations'.
Point 1 (1 mark): she cared for the garden while he was away and brought the wilting plants back to health / made the garden more beautiful than ever.
Point 2 (1 mark): she kept a detailed notebook of careful observations.
Say what Maya DID (her actions), not just how the garden looked.

review.keyAnswer: Maya cared for the garden while her grandfather was in hospital, restored the wilted and aphid-attacked plants to health, and kept a detailed notebook of what she did.
review.solvedAnswer: She looked after the garden while he was away so that the plants were healthy and the garden more beautiful than ever, and kept a detailed notebook of observations. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: How had Mother's opinion of Maya changed by the end of the story?

answer.value: At first, Mother was concerned that Maya would not be able to handle the big responsibility of taking care of the garden. By the end of the story, she was impressed by and approved of what Maya had done, as she nodded and gave Maya a thumbs-up.

explanation: A 'how did it change' question needs both sides: the opinion before (1 mark) and the opinion after (1 mark).
